To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of red cell surface antigens influences the rate of erythrocytic clearance by splenic Fc receptors but that IC inhibit the clearance of erythrocyts sensitized with a single antigenic site.

the number of red blood cell antigens on the cell surface influences the clearance of antibody coated cells by splenic macro-phages but not their susceptibility towards immune complex inhibition of clearance.

the spleen is the principal organ responsible for the clearance of erythrocytic immune complexes in the rat, that immune complexes can inhibit the clearance of erythrophages from the spleen, that this inhibition is dependent on the presence of the Fc portion of the antibody, and that the rate of erythrophagocytosis in the spleen is dependent on the number of antigens on the cell surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the spleen in immune complex disease.
the study of immune complex formation and its effects on the clearance of erythrocytic antigen-antibody complexes.
the influence of soluble immune complexes on the splenic component of mononuclear phgocyte system (Mps).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IC formed with the Fc fragment of an antibody inhibit the clearance of antibody coated erythocytes by the spleen.
IC inhibit erythrocyte coated with R3/ 13 antibody in the presence of complement.
IC formed at antigen excess inhibit Fc receptor dependent erythrocyte phagocytosis by the spleen and the degree of the inhibition depends on the amount of IC present in the plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
immune complexes formed with the whole antibody, at antigen excess, inhibit the splenic clearance of erythrocyts sensitized with R 3/13 antibody by the splenic component of MPS.
the spleen is a major organ of the MPS in the rat and the Fc receptor is the most sensitive marker of splenic macrophages.
immune complexes formed at 10-fold excess of antigen to antibody, inhibit the splenic component of Fc receptor function, but not Fc receptor function on the Kupffer cells of the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spleen is an important component of the MPS.
it is important to consider the number of specific surface antigens on a target cell when assessing the clearance of sensitised cells.

the number of red blood cell antigens influences the rate atwhich sensitized cells are cleared by splenic macro-phages but does not influence their susceptibility to inhibition of clearance by soluble immune complexes.
